acceptance.given: A historical replay input includes binding identities that differ from the identities reconstructed from its replay inputs.

oracle.expected: The replay validator reconstructs the historical binding identity, compares it with replay-input identities, and terminates with rejection without producing a replay result.
forbidden: Proceeding with mismatched historical replay bindings.
Treating identity mismatch as a valid replay.
Claiming replay equivalence from mismatched inputs.
oracle.observable: A machine-readable terminal rejection records the binding mismatch and no replay-result artifact is emitted.

acceptance.then: The replay binding check has completed.
acceptance.when: When validating historical replay input bindings.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the historical replay binding test with a deliberately mismatched binding identity and require the runtime marker to show rejection; a pass indicates the implementation incorrectly proceeds.
Run the replay binding test with altered replay inputs and verify that reconstructed identity differs and blocks replay; accepting supplied or stale identity is a target-binding failure.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reconstruct the original historical binding identity before replay, replay only with that same identity, and reject identity-mismatched inputs without emitting a replay result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay-result categories and reject mismatches without altering historical records.

slice_hint.state_transition: binding identity reconstructed -> identities compared -> mismatch terminally rejected; no replay result state is created.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Terminal failure is reached iff reconstructed historical binding identity differs from replay-input identity; no replay-result artifact exists.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result has reached successful status and includes a command invocation record.

oracle.expected: The successful Replay Result contains independently obtained verification of the command identity and execution, bound to the same replay result.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result without independent command verification.
oracle.observable: The replay-result evidence contains an independent command-verification record whose identity matches the executed command and whose provenance is separate from the success claim.

acceptance.then: Independent command verification has been recorded for the successful result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the successful replay-result test with independent command verification removed or falsified and require the runtime marker to reject the result.
Run the replay-result evidence check against a result whose command proof is copied from the success payload rather than independently collected; copied provenance must fail integrity validation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require every successful Replay Result to bind an independently verified command identity and execution record before success is accepted.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing successful result schemas remain readable; missing independent command proof changes the terminal result to unsuccessful.

slice_hint.state_transition: replay execution -> independent command verification -> success publication only when verification is bound.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A success terminal state is valid iff independent command verification is present and identity-consistent; otherwise result is rejected as evidence-invalid.

acceptance.given: A native command identity exists before repair and the repair workflow is executed.

oracle.expected: The before-and-after comparison shows the native command identity is byte-for-byte unchanged.
forbidden: Replacing or changing the identity of a native command
oracle.observable: A deterministic comparison artifact records equal native command identities before and after repair and reports no mutation.

acceptance.then: Native command identity remains unchanged after repair.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the native-command identity comparison against a deliberately changed command identity and require deterministic constraint failure.
Run the identity-preservation check with the before or after identity absent; absence of comparison evidence must fail closed.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve and compare the native command identity across repair without replacement, normalization, or substitution.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Historical command identity remains authoritative as immutable evidence; repair comparison is append-only.

slice_hint.state_transition: capture pre-repair identity -> perform repair -> capture post-repair identity -> compare unchanged.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Constraint passes only when pre- and post-repair native command identities are equal and comparison evidence is complete.

acceptance.given: A TC-D1 write request targets a runtime boundary path.

oracle.expected: The Toolchain write-scope guard rejects the request before any runtime-boundary file is modified.
forbidden: Writing to runtime paths as part of TC-D1 work.
Treating runtime repair as authorized by replay or Consumer permission.
oracle.observable: The guard emits a deterministic rejection identifying the protected runtime boundary and the attempted write is absent from the post-check tree.

acceptance.then: Runtime boundaries remain protected from TC-D1 writes.
acceptance.when: When a TC-D1 write targets a runtime path.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Invoke the write-scope validator with a runtime path target and require the guard to reject; any allowed write is a governance contract failure.
Invoke the validator with a canonical runtime boundary path and verify it is classified as protected rather than as an ordinary Toolchain path.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a hard write boundary that rejects TC-D1 attempts to modify runtime paths before mutation, independent of replay or Consumer permissions.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Write-scope enforcement remains fail-closed and does not mutate runtime state or authorize exceptions.

slice_hint.state_transition: write request classified -> runtime boundary detected -> request rejected -> filesystem unchanged.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Terminal rejection is required whenever the resolved target is within a runtime boundary; no runtime file change is permitted.
